pr_title: ES|QL: Add random test query generator
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/98768

~~DO NOT MERGE, fix below issues first!~~

Add a test that iteratively generates random queries starting from test indexes (CSV tests).
It's just string manipulation to create syntactically valid queries, no semantics at all (hence no validation of the results).
The intention is to test errors and corner cases in query planning and layout management, plus to spot wrongly managed exceptions.

Tests disabled by default, because there are still some known issues in the query planner that trigger failures.

Problems found: 

- [x] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/102061
- [x] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/102084
- [x] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/102083
- [x] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/102120
- [x] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/102121
- [x] https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/102123

issue_context.title: ES|QL testing: random query generator/test
issue_context.body:
To catch corner cases like https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/98404, it could be useful to have some kind of random query generator/test.

A simple proposal:
1. map all the supported commands/expressions/functions  and the available test indexes
2. map all the expected errors (Eg. validation exceptions)
3. define a `<max-depth>` for the generated queries
4. generate a one-command query (Eg. `from <random-index-pattern>`) based on the available indexes
5. run the query 
4.1. if it throws a valid error, return and succeed
4.2. if it throws an unexpected error, fail
4.3 if the query is `<max-depth>` commands deep, return and succeed
6. based on the query output (field names, maybe types; ignore the actual results), randomly generate a syntactically valid command using the mappings in (1) and append it to the query
7. iterate to (5)


Goals:
- catch unexpected exceptions and corner cases (layout errors, assertion errors, NPE, data loading problems, blind spots on query planning)
- rationalize the query errors (see point 2)

Non-goals:
- validate the results: since the query generation is randomized, checking the correctness of the results is out of scope

review_comments: Same for `keep`: add some wildcards here and there.
